title: What We're Looking For
subtitle: Screening variables for serial acquirers / M&A compounders — distilled from Thorndike, Mauboussin, Demesne, Swedish compounder operators, and investor letters/X discourse.
sources: X / letters: AcquirerHQ, PrivatEquityGuy, ValueByMarkus, Compounding Quality, Dutch Investors, Quartr

pillars.name: Proven deal machine
lookFor: Many small, repeatable acquisitions vs rare mega-deals
Decades of compounding via M&A (or clear inheritance of the playbook)
High hit rate; few large write-downs or forced disposals
Management that talks about process, hurdles, and kill criteria — not just 'synergies'
redFlags: Frequent impairment charges after big integrations

pillars.name: Multiple arbitrage
lookFor: Buys private/niche assets at low EV/EBITDA (often high-single to low-teens) while public vehicle trades richer
Fragmented sellers (founder exits, succession) with weak auction processes
Ability to keep paying modest multiples even as the platform scales
redFlags: Paying public-market multiples for private assets
Auction-driven bidding wars becoming the norm

pillars.name: 1+1 > 2 (value creation beyond buying)
lookFor: Either: autonomy model (preserve culture, keep talent, light HQ) — Swedish/CSU style
Or: disciplined cost/operating leverage (procurement, shared services) without destroying the niche
Pricing power, cross-sell, or 'complete solution' bundling where real (e.g. Danaher bioprocess)
Evidence that acquired ROIC stays high post-close
redFlags: Heavy centralization that kills niche entrepreneurship

pillars.name: Acquisition runway
lookFor: Still-fragmented end markets with thousands of small targets
Niche critical products/software (VMS, safety, dental, scientific instruments)
Addressable pipeline disclosed or inferable from deal pace vs market size
redFlags: TAM exhausted; forced into larger/riskier deals
Category consolidating into oligopoly with no small targets left

pillars.name: Capital allocation discipline
lookFor: Explicit hierarchy: M&A vs organic reinvestment vs buybacks vs dividends vs debt paydown
Willingness to sit on cash when prices are high
Share count discipline; limited serial dilution
Returns on incremental capital / ROIIC tracked and discussed
redFlags: Constant equity issuance to fund mediocre deals

pillars.name: Incentives & decentralization
lookFor: Owner-operators or strong owner mindset
Local P&L accountability; acquired managers stay and earn equity/earnouts aligned to value
HQ as capital allocator, not operating micromanager
Succession plan for the capital allocator (CEO stress test)
redFlags: Incentives tied only to revenue or deal count

pillars.name: Cash & accounting quality
lookFor: High cash conversion after earnouts and working capital
Organic vs acquired growth separable
Goodwill growth matched by cash returns, not just EPS optics
Prudent leverage — tool, not requirement
redFlags: Rising leverage + rising purchase multiples together
Cash earnings chronically lag reported earnings

scoreGuide.description: Initial ranks score each company 1–10 on the seven pillars above, then form a weighted total (0–100). User ranks override defaults and persist in the browser.

tiers.label: Elite compounder
tiers.note: Deep track record, durable runway, proven capital allocation

tiers.label: Strong platform
tiers.note: Clear model; watch valuation and succession

tiers.label: Watchlist quality
tiers.note: Fits the framework; needs more seasoning or valuation patience

tiers.label: Speculative / early
tiers.note: Model nascent, cyclical, or execution risk elevated
